artifact: The bar a consolidated food search has to clear, pre-registered before the membership rule exists (#188).
conditions_note: Two conditions, asking two different questions. C1 is the user-facing one: is the row a diarist means near the top. C2 exists only to stop C1 being passed dishonestly - a ninth ranking key could lift a gold row into the top 3 while the query still answers with 954 rows, which is the map's destination missed. Result-set size is the one number ranking cannot move: reorder 954 rows and there are still 954. Only dropping or merging changes it.

c1_gold_in_top_3.rule: For every gating query, the gold row appears in the first three results of the shipped search.
c1_gold_in_top_3.baseline_note: Measured at registration; see the note.

c2_result_set_cap.rule: No gating query returns more than 25 rows.
c2_result_set_cap.cap_note: Chosen from the distribution, not after seeing a rule's output: clear of the 50-row page cap, just above the roster median of 14, and flat between 20 and 30 (18/17/16 of 45 failing), so the exact figure is not delicate.

corpus_size.rule: SANITY ONLY - no pass or fail attached.
corpus_size.rule_note: CORRECTED 2026-09-12 by issue 190, see section 8 of the note; registered as [1850, 1900]. The registered zone came from a crude DROP (delete every row naming a cooking method, then every row naming a trim or grade), which deletes 2,404 rows of which 2,181 leave a residual group with no survivor at all, taking 18 head phrases out entirely including quinoa, teff, spelt, mutton and apricots. A rule ADR-0055 section 1 permits COLLAPSES instead and lands at 2,923 residual groups before any head phrase is adjudicated. A rule landing far outside this range is asked to explain itself; a rule landing inside it and failing C1 or C2 still fails.

gold_set_note: Keyed by fdcId, with the description carried alongside as a human label only. Descriptions are NOT the key: ADR-0056's shipped-name work renames rows, so a description-keyed gold set would silently report a renamed row as missing - which is exactly the failure that produced three false 'not in corpus' readings while this set was being written.
gold_set_amendments_note: A pre-registered bar loses its point if the gold set can be edited to make a result look better, so every change to it is recorded here with its reason, and the reason has to be that the FOOD moved rather than that the SCORE did.

was: Rice, white, long grain, unenriched, raw
gold_set_amendments.why: The pinned row left the corpus, and the bar reported a BROKEN BAR rather than a miss, which is the right behaviour and why it is being answered rather than ignored. It was not dropped: ADR-0101's enrichment rule collided it with `Rice, white, long-grain, regular, raw, unenriched` and kept one row for the two, which is a collapse leaving a survivor - the operation ADR-0100 permits, as against a drop, which it does not. 168877 IS that survivor, and it ships under the name a reader asked for in as many words.
gold_set_amendments.not_a_goalpost_move: C1 asks whether the row a diarist means is near the top. A diarist means long-grain white rice; that food is still in the corpus and still one row. Re-pinning to the survivor keeps the question the same - and it is worth saying plainly that this repin takes C1 from 24/44 to 25/44, so it is a change that FLATTERS the result and has to be read with that in mind. The alternative, leaving a pin on a row that no longer exists, measures nothing at all.

one_word.description: Beef, ground, 80% lean meat / 20% fat, raw
Pork, fresh, loin, whole, separable lean and fat, raw

one_word.note: The corpus ships no plain bacon; this is the nearest, and it leads today. A near-hole recorded rather than hidden.

one_word.description: Pork, cured, ham, whole, separable lean and fat, unheated
one_word.note: Typing `ham` returns ONE row (Ham, sliced, restaurant) while `gammon` returns 88, because ADR-0062's stray-mention rule drops rows the typed word reaches only past the food's own name. The cured hams ship and are unreachable by their own word.

one_word.description: Turkey, breast, meat and skin, raw
Fish, salmon, Atlantic, farm raised, raw

one_word.note: No canned tuna ships, so the gold is the commonest fresh one.

one_word.description: Eggs, Grade A, Large, egg whole
one_word.note: The plain raw hen's egg, a Foundation row carrying `Egg, whole, raw, fresh` as an ADR-0050 twin alias. Present and correctly merged; it loses to duck, goose, quail and turkey.

one_word.description: Bread, white, commercially prepared (includes soft bread crumbs)
Oats, whole grain, rolled, old fashioned
Tomatoes, red, ripe, raw, year round average

one_word.note: The row leading today is `Mushroom, white, exposed to ultraviolet light, raw` - the same mushroom wearing a qualifier nobody means.
No plain `Apples, raw` ships; gala is the most-grown variety and stands in for it.

one_word.description: Bananas, ripe and slightly ripe, raw
Beans, kidney, red, mature seeds, raw
one_word.note: CONTESTABLE. `beans` has no single answer a diarist agrees on - baked, green and kidney are three different logs. Kidney is picked as the commonest pulse and the choice is recorded as arguable rather than presented as obvious.

excluded.reason: A genuine coverage hole. The corpus ships no chocolate: the rows a `chocolate` query reaches are two cocoa beverage powders and three ice creams. There is no row a diarist means, so there is no gold row, and a query that can only fail for a reason the membership rule cannot fix would make the pilot read worse than it is. Excluded with its reason on the record rather than scored.

british_tripwire_note: NOT a pass condition and NOT a ticket on this map. British words reach food by a different machine - ADR-0049's vocabulary, 444 OFF-derived expansions plus 8 hand-written local ones - and 15 of these 17 match no corpus row literally. They are carried only so the pilot notices a silent breakage: ADR-0049's map is derived FROM corpus text, and three of these queries are one row away from returning nothing. The test is only 'did a query that returned something now return nothing'.

british_tripwire.correction: CORRECTED 2026-09-12 by issue 190: registered as 50, which was a page-capped hits.length reading rather than an answer size. The tripwire fires on a fall to zero, so its verdict is unchanged.

british_tripwire.note: FRAGILE - one row. Drop `Oats, whole grain, rolled, old fashioned` and this answers with nothing.

multi_word_note: Watched on its own denominator, NOT gating. #151 established that a head-phrase-only sweep cannot price a multi-word rule, so these are carried to catch a rule that fixes one-word queries by breaking two-word ones.
